headline: Two youths confess to raping and killing a child, body dumped in canal

headline: Tk 11 trillion: Risky loans in banking sector hit 59.73% of total disbursements
summary: Bangladesh Bank's Financial Stability Report 2025 reveals a massive surge in risky loans, with non-performing loans alone reaching Tk 5.88 trillion.
details: Bangladesh Bank reports that nearly Tk 11 trillion in loans from the banking sector are currently at risk or facing difficulties. This amount accounts for 59.73 percent of all loans disbursed, according to the Financial Stability Report 2025.
Non-performing loans (NPLs) have climbed to Tk 5.88 trillion, increasing by Tk 314.87 billion in just three months. Year-on-year, risky loans grew by Tk 3.31 trillion from Tk 7.57 trillion in 2024.

The central bank classifies defaulted, written-off, and rescheduled loans as 'risky.' Of the total risky loans, defaulted loans stand at Tk 5.57 trillion, while refinanced loans are at Tk 4.47 trillion and written-off loans at Tk 834.79 billion.

A record Tk 1.71 trillion was refinanced in 2025 alone, more than double the Tk 850 billion refinanced in the previous year. Additionally, Tk 1.82 trillion in loans under High Court bans cannot be categorized as non-performing.

The surge in risky assets has caused the capital adequacy ratio to drop from 3 percent to 2.64 percent. The banking sector also faces a significant loan provisioning deficit of Tk 1.91 trillion, having maintained only Tk 2.49 trillion of the required Tk 4.41 trillion.
caption:
Nearly 60% of all bank loans in Bangladesh are now considered 'risky.' 

Tk 11 trillion is currently at risk or facing difficulty.

Bangladesh Bank reports that nearly Tk 11 trillion in loans from the banking sector are currently at risk or facing difficulties. This amount accounts for 59.73 percent of all loans disbursed, according to the Financial Stability Report 2025.

Non-performing loans (NPLs) have climbed to Tk 5.88 trillion, increasing by Tk 314.87 billion in just three months. Year-on-year, risky loans grew by Tk 3.31 trillion from Tk 7.57 trillion in 2024.

The central bank classifies defaulted, written-off, and rescheduled loans as 'risky.' Of the total risky loans, defaulted loans stand at Tk 5.57 trillion, while refinanced loans are at Tk 4.47 trillion and written-off loans at Tk 834.79 billion.

A record Tk 1.71 trillion was refinanced in 2025 alone, more than double the Tk 850 billion refinanced in the previous year. Additionally, Tk 1.82 trillion in loans under High Court bans cannot be categorized as non-performing.

The surge in risky assets has caused the capital adequacy ratio to drop from 3 percent to 2.64 percent. The banking sector also faces a significant loan provisioning deficit of Tk 1.91 trillion, having maintained only Tk 2.49 trillion of the required Tk 4.41 trillion.
